# Views and components

`Markup.view`: drawing elements in a window, pressing, components, loaders and progress bars.

## markup.view

Source: `lua/markup/view/init.lua`

Fields:

- `CONTEXT`: `string` - Context key that holds the view of the current component.

### markup.view:after_commit()

```lua
markup.view:after_commit(listener: function)
```

Calls `listener` after the next commit.

### markup.view:apply()

```lua
markup.view:apply(patches: table[])
  -> lines: integer
```

Patch ranges refer to the previous frame, so last to first keeps them valid.

### markup.view:attach()

```lua
markup.view:attach()
```

Starts over from a blank buffer, which the engine's next frame then fills.

### markup.view:click()

```lua
markup.view:click(mouse: table, kind?: "double"|"single")
  -> pressed: boolean
```

Presses what is under the mouse, which `mouse` from `getmousepos()` points at,
if it takes this kind of click.

```lua
kind:
   | "single"
   | "double"
```

### markup.view:columns()

```lua
markup.view:columns()
  -> integer
```

Width of the window. Reading it tracks resizes.

### markup.view:commit()

```lua
markup.view:commit()
```

Sends pending commands and applies the resulting patches.

```lua
function markup.view.commit_job()
```

### markup.view:destroy()

```lua
markup.view:destroy()
```

Stops everything and forgets the view. The window is left to its owner.

### markup.view.find()

```lua
function markup.view.find(win?: integer)
  -> (markup.view)?
```

The view shown in a window, or the first one in the current tab.

### markup.view:height()

```lua
markup.view:height()
  -> integer
```

Height to lay out for, which hidden windows can only estimate.

### markup.view:hold_cursor()

```lua
markup.view:hold_cursor(at?: integer[])
  -> release: fun()
```

Keeps the cursor where it is while what is under it moves, such as during
a transition: rows added above it do not carry it along, nothing snaps it
onto what passes by, and nothing is hovered. `at` is where it waits, its
`{ row, col }` as `nvim_win_get_cursor` gives it, where it is by default.
Returns a function that lets it go, which snaps it to the nearest node.

### markup.view:on_commit()

```lua

```

Calls `listener` after every commit.

### markup.view:place_held()

```lua
markup.view:place_held()
```

Puts a held cursor back where it waits, after lines moved it.

### markup.view:place_images()

```lua
markup.view:place_images()
```

Shows each image over its box, moves it with the box, and takes it away
when the box is out of sight or cut, since an image cannot be cut, or when a
float is over it.

### markup.view:press()

```lua
markup.view:press()
  -> boolean
```

Calls the `on_press` handler under the cursor, returning whether there was one.

### markup.view:release_cursor()

```lua
markup.view:release_cursor()
```

Shows the cursor again, if this view hid it.

### markup.view:render()

```lua
markup.view:render(content: any)
```

Replaces what the view shows. `content` is rendered once, and stays live
until the next call or until `unmount`.

## markup.view.components

Source: `lua/markup/view/components.lua`

Fields:

- `loaders`: `table<string, markup.view.loader_def>` - Animated marks for work in progress, each one cell wide. Some spin, others fill, grow, fade or bloom. Those marked `nerd_font` need a Nerd Font; `pick` draws from some of them.
- `spinners`: `table<string, markup.view.loader_def>` - The names from before there were loaders that do not spin, kept for the plugins that use them.

### markup.view.components.bar()

```lua
function markup.view.components.bar(value: number, width: integer)
  -> string
```

The text of a bar, with eighths of a cell of precision.

### markup.view.components.loader()

```lua
function markup.view.components.loader(props?: markup.view.loader)
  -> unknown
```

An animated character that runs for as long as it is shown.

### markup.view.components.loader_names()

```lua
function markup.view.components.loader_names(pick?: markup.view.loader_pick)
  -> string[]
```

Names of the loaders, in a stable order: all of them, or those `pick`
allows.

### markup.view.components.loader_width()

```lua
function markup.view.components.loader_width(loader: markup.view.loader_def)
  -> integer
```

How many cells the widest frame of a loader takes.

### markup.view.components.progress()

```lua
function markup.view.components.progress(props: markup.view.progress)
  -> markup.element
```

A bar that shows fractions of a cell, so it can move smoothly.

## markup.view.loader

Source: `lua/markup/view/components.lua`

Fields:

- `interval`: `integer?` - ms per frame
- `name`: `string?` - one of `loaders`, a random one by default
- `pick`: `(markup.view.loader_pick)?` - which loaders the random one is drawn from
- `style`: `string?`

## markup.view.loader_def

Source: `lua/markup/view/components.lua`

Fields:

- `frames`: `string[]`
- `interval`: `integer` - ms per frame
- `nerd_font`: `true?` - needs a Nerd Font to show

## markup.view.loader_pick

Source: `lua/markup/view/components.lua`

Fields:

- `names`: `string[]?` - only these loaders
- `nerd_font`: `boolean?` - true for only the loaders that need a Nerd Font, false for only those that do not
- `width`: `integer?` - only the loaders this many cells wide

## markup.view.opts

Source: `lua/markup/view/init.lua`

Fields:

- `hide_cursor`: `boolean?` - hide the cursor in normal mode while in this window,
- `snap`: `(boolean|"text")?` - keep the cursor on interactive nodes, like a menu,

## markup.view.progress

Source: `lua/markup/view/components.lua`

Fields:

- `style`: `string?` - color of the bar
- `track`: `string?` - background behind it
- `value`: `number|fun():number` - from 0 to 1
- `width`: `integer`
